body: Ye’s “Graduation” turns 19 today 🎓🐻💜 Released on September 11, 2007, the album gave us “Stronger,” “Good Life,” “Can’t Tell Me Nothing,” “Flashing Lights,” “I Wonder” and so many more songs that still feel just as good almost two decades later. 🔥 For his third album, Kanye expanded his sound with bright synths, electronic influences and huge hooks. Paired with Takashi Murakami’s unmistakable artwork, “Graduation” had an identity you could recognize before you even pressed play. Its release also brought one of hip-hop’s most memorable sales battles, going head-to-head with 50 Cent’s “Curtis.” “Graduation” debuted at No. 1 with approximately 957,000 copies sold in its first week in the U.S. 🤯 But beyond the numbers, it’s the songs that keep people coming back. Whether it’s the opening of “Good Morning” or singing every word of “I Wonder,” this album holds a different memory for everybody. What’s your favorite song on “Graduation”? 👇 📸: Brad Barket / Getty images

Ye’s “Graduation” turns 19 today 🎓🐻💜

Released on September 11, 2007, the album gave us “Stronger,” “Good Life,” “Can’t Tell Me Nothing,” “Flashing Lights,” “I Wonder” and so many more songs that still feel just as good almost two decades later. 🔥

For his third album, Kanye expanded his sound with bright synths, electronic influences and huge hooks. Paired with Takashi Murakami’s unmistakable artwork, “Graduation” had an identity you could recognize before you even pressed play.

Its release also brought one of hip-hop’s most memorable sales battles, going head-to-head with 50 Cent’s “Curtis.” “Graduation” debuted at No. 1 with approximately 957,000 copies sold in its first week in the U.S. 🤯

But beyond the numbers, it’s the songs that keep people coming back. Whether it’s the opening of “Good Morning” or singing every word of “I Wonder,” this album holds a different memory for everybody.
